entries.text: Under dynamic shapes, expressions such as 0.95 ** x.shape[0] are lowered to ops.index_expr(FloatPow(0.95, ToFloat(s77))). MetalExprPrinter had no _print_FloatPow, so codegen fell through to the base printer and raised NotImplementedError, breaking e.g. Adam-style bias correction (1 - beta ** step) under torch.compile(dynamic=True) on MPS. Alias it to _print_PowByNatural, which already casts both operands to float and emits metal::precise::pow, mirroring the C++ (std::pow) and Triton (libdevice.pow) printers. Add test_float_pow_symint_exponent, the reproducer from the issue, as a regression test. Fixes #206879 Authored with an AI assistant (Claude Code). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 noreply@anthropic.com Pull Request resolved: #206922 Approved by: https://github.com/pytorchgreenlight, https://github.com/Isalia20

entries.text: Summary (human written only) We want to add more pyobject converters! (This would enable people to use stable APIs even when registering through nanobind vs being forced to go through the dispatcher.) This stack does that, the files they update are organized as such: Agent details (if applicable) AI-generated Summary Add 2.16+ Layout from/to-Python helpers and the initial libtorch-only ABI3 interop fixture. The runtime Layout code crosses the C shim and is translated through the existing stable enum mapping rather than freezing header-only enum values. Ownership expectation (AI-generated) Python to C++: borrow the Python torch.layout input and return a Layout enum value; no Python reference or borrowed Python storage escapes into that value. C++ to Python: return a new owning reference to the registered layout singleton. This acquires a reference, not a new instance; the caller must release or transfer it, and it does not retain the C++ input. Tensor integration: the temporary stable Tensor owns a native handle sharing its TensorImpl. The returned layout reference is independent of that temporary Tensor's lifetime; tensor data is not copied. The caller keeps borrowed inputs alive for the call. Python-object operations and reference cleanup require the GIL and a loaded libtorch_python backend. Compatibility and ownership Inputs are borrowed actual torch.layout objects; outputs are owned references to the registered singleton. Calls require the GIL and libtorch_python loaded at

entries.text: Summary (human written only) As title, memory format is like layout Agent details (if applicable) AI-generated Summary Add 2.16+ MemoryFormat from/to-Python helpers using runtime codes and the existing stable enum translation, matching the Layout bridge. Ownership expectation (AI-generated) Python to C++: borrow the Python torch.memory_format input and return a MemoryFormat enum value, independent of the input object's lifetime after conversion. C++ to Python: acquire a new owning reference to the existing registered memory-format singleton, rather than allocate a duplicate. The caller releases or transfers that reference; no C++ input is retained. The caller keeps borrowed inputs alive for the call. Python-object operations and reference cleanup require the GIL and a loaded libtorch_python backend. Compatibility and ownership Require actual torch.memory_format input and return an owned reference to its registered singleton. Borrowed inputs and GIL/runtime requirements are unchanged. Test plan and evidence Full-stack native validation passed 67 cases without skips: 23 existing and 41 new PyObject cases, two RNG regressions and the concurrent Generator identity/retirement case. All four strengthened exception-message assertions passed. The final incremental pip update, runtime tests, 15 installed-header checks, 20 shim-export checks and three interop ELF audits passed. Interop modules link only libc10/libtorch/libtorch_cpu among torch libraries, not libtorch_python. Unchanged
